KJV.text: The Lord is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the Lord hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
KJV.displayText: The Lord is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the Lord hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.

BSB.text: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.
BSB.displayText: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.

CPDV.text: The Lord is patient and great in strength, and those who are not clean, he makes innocent. The Lord is in a tempest, and his way is a whirlwind, and the clouds are dust at his feet.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord is patient and great in strength, and those who are not clean, he makes innocent. The Lord is in a tempest, and his way is a whirlwind, and the clouds are dust at his feet.

verses.context: Opening his message against Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, Nahum describes God as slow to anger yet great in power, never leaving guilt unpunished.

KJV.text: What do ye imagine against the Lord? he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.
KJV.displayText: What do ye imagine against the Lord? he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.

BSB.text: Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end. Affliction will not rise up a second time.
BSB.displayText: Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end. Affliction will not rise up a second time.

CPDV.text: What are you thinking up against the Lord? He will accomplish the consummation. There shall not rise up a double tribulation.
CPDV.displayText: What are you thinking up against the Lord? He will accomplish the consummation. There shall not rise up a double tribulation.

verses.context: Announcing Nineveh's fall, Nahum tells those who plot against the Lord that God will finish them, so the trouble they brought will not rise again.

KJV.text: Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.
KJV.displayText: Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.

BSB.text: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
BSB.displayText: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.

CPDV.text: Because of this, the law has been torn apart, and judgment does not persevere to its conclusion. For the impious prevail against the just. Because of this, a perverse judgment is issued.
CPDV.displayText: Because of this, the law has been torn apart, and judgment does not persevere to its conclusion. For the impious prevail against the just. Because of this, a perverse judgment is issued.

verses.context: In his opening complaint, Habakkuk tells God that violence has spread so far in Judah that the law is paralyzed and justice is twisted.

KJV.text: Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you.
KJV.displayText: Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you.

BSB.text: “Look at the nations and observe— be utterly astounded! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe even if someone told you.
BSB.displayText: “Look at the nations and observe— be utterly astounded! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe even if someone told you.

CPDV.text: Gaze among the nations, and see. Admire, and be astounded. For a work has been done in your days, which no one will believe when it is told.
CPDV.displayText: Gaze among the nations, and see. Admire, and be astounded. For a work has been done in your days, which no one will believe when it is told.

verses.context: Answering Habakkuk's complaint about injustice, God says he is about to do something unbelievable: raise up the Babylonians to bring judgment.

KJV.text: Art thou not from everlasting, O Lord my God, mine Holy One? we shall not die. O Lord, thou hast ordained them for judgment; and, O mighty God, thou hast established them for correction.
KJV.displayText: Art thou not from everlasting, O Lord my God, mine Holy One? we shall not die. O Lord, thou hast ordained them for judgment; and, O mighty God, thou hast established them for correction.

BSB.text: Are You not from everlasting, O LORD, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. O LORD, You have appointed them to execute judgment; O Rock, You have established them for correction.
BSB.displayText: Are You not from everlasting, O LORD, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. O LORD, You have appointed them to execute judgment; O Rock, You have established them for correction.

CPDV.text: Have you not existed from the beginning, Lord my God, my holy one, and so we shall not die? Lord, you have stationed him for judgment, and you have established that his strength will be swept away.
CPDV.displayText: Have you not existed from the beginning, Lord my God, my holy one, and so we shall not die? Lord, you have stationed him for judgment, and you have established that his strength will be swept away.

verses.context: Troubled that God would use the ruthless Babylonians to bring judgment, Habakkuk appeals to God as everlasting, his Holy One and his Rock.

KJV.text: And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.
KJV.displayText: And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.

BSB.text: Then the LORD answered me: “Write down this vision and clearly inscribe it on tablets, so that a herald may run with it.
BSB.displayText: Then the LORD answered me: “Write down this vision and clearly inscribe it on tablets, so that a herald may run with it.

CPDV.text: And the Lord responded to me and said: Write the vision and explain it on tablets, so that he who reads it may run through it.
CPDV.displayText: And the Lord responded to me and said: Write the vision and explain it on tablets, so that he who reads it may run through it.

verses.context: After Habakkuk takes his post on the watchtower to wait for an answer, God tells him to write the vision down plainly so a messenger can run with it.

KJV.text: When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.
KJV.displayText: When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.

BSB.text: I heard and trembled within; my lips quivered at the sound. Decay entered my bones; I trembled where I stood. Yet I must wait patiently for the day of distress to come upon the people who invade us.
BSB.displayText: I heard and trembled within; my lips quivered at the sound. Decay entered my bones; I trembled where I stood. Yet I must wait patiently for the day of distress to come upon the people who invade us.

CPDV.text: I heard, and my stomach became troubled. My lips trembled at the voice. Let decay enter into my bones and gush forth from within me. Then I may rest in the day of tribulation, so that I may ascend to our people well-prepared.
CPDV.displayText: I heard, and my stomach became troubled. My lips trembled at the voice. Let decay enter into my bones and gush forth from within me. Then I may rest in the day of tribulation, so that I may ascend to our people well-prepared.

verses.context: After a vision of God marching out to save his people, Habakkuk trembles to his bones, yet resolves to wait quietly for the day of distress.

KJV.text: Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.
KJV.displayText: Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.

BSB.text: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the earth who carry out His justice. Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD’s anger.
BSB.displayText: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the earth who carry out His justice. Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD’s anger.

CPDV.text: Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth; you who have been working are his judgment. Seek the just, seek the meek. So then, in some way, you might be hidden in the day of the fury of the Lord.
CPDV.displayText: Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth; you who have been working are his judgment. Seek the just, seek the meek. So then, in some way, you might be hidden in the day of the fury of the Lord.

verses.context: Warning Judah that the day of the Lord's anger is near, Zephaniah urges the humble of the earth to seek righteousness and humility while there is still time.

KJV.text: In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain.
KJV.displayText: In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain.

BSB.text: On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me. For then I will remove from among you those who rejoice in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on My holy mountain.
BSB.displayText: On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me. For then I will remove from among you those who rejoice in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on My holy mountain.

CPDV.text: In that day, you will not be ashamed over all of your inventions, by which you have transgressed against me. For then I will take away from your midst your arrogant boasters, and you will no longer be exalted on my holy mountain.
CPDV.displayText: In that day, you will not be ashamed over all of your inventions, by which you have transgressed against me. For then I will take away from your midst your arrogant boasters, and you will no longer be exalted on my holy mountain.

verses.context: Looking beyond judgment on Jerusalem, Zephaniah promises that the city will no longer be shamed by its past sins once God removes the proud from its midst.

KJV.text: I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.
KJV.displayText: I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.

BSB.text: But I will leave within you a meek and humble people, and they will trust in the name of the LORD.
BSB.displayText: But I will leave within you a meek and humble people, and they will trust in the name of the LORD.

CPDV.text: And I will bequeath into your midst a poor and needy people, and they will hope in the name of the Lord.
CPDV.displayText: And I will bequeath into your midst a poor and needy people, and they will hope in the name of the Lord.

verses.context: Once the proud are removed from Jerusalem, Zephaniah says, God will leave in the city a meek and lowly people who trust in his name.

KJV.text: At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord.
KJV.displayText: At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord.

BSB.text: At that time I will bring you in; yes, at that time I will gather you. For I will give you fame and praise among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your captives before your very eyes,” says the LORD.
BSB.displayText: At that time I will bring you in; yes, at that time I will gather you. For I will give you fame and praise among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your captives before your very eyes,” says the LORD.

CPDV.text: in that time, when I will lead to you, and in the time when I will gather for you. For I will deliver you into renown and into praise, among all the peoples of the earth, when I will have converted your captivity before your very eyes, says the Lord.
CPDV.displayText: in that time, when I will lead to you, and in the time when I will gather for you. For I will deliver you into renown and into praise, among all the peoples of the earth, when I will have converted your captivity before your very eyes, says the Lord.

verses.context: In the last line of Zephaniah's prophecy, God promises to gather his scattered people home and make them honored among all the nations.

KJV.text: Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.
KJV.displayText: Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.

BSB.text: You have planted much but harvested little. You eat but never have enough. You drink but never have your fill. You put on clothes but never get warm. You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.”
BSB.displayText: You have planted much but harvested little. You eat but never have enough. You drink but never have your fill. You put on clothes but never get warm. You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.”

CPDV.text: You sowed much and have brought in little. You consumed and have not been satisfied. You drank and have not been inebriated. You covered yourselves and have not been warmed. And whoever gathered wages, has put them in a bag with holes.
CPDV.displayText: You sowed much and have brought in little. You consumed and have not been satisfied. You drank and have not been inebriated. You covered yourselves and have not been warmed. And whoever gathered wages, has put them in a bag with holes.

verses.context: Rebuking returned exiles who lived in fine houses while the temple lay in ruins, Haggai points out that all their hard work never leaves them satisfied.

KJV.text: Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?
KJV.displayText: Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?

BSB.text: ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not appear to you like nothing in comparison?’
BSB.displayText: ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not appear to you like nothing in comparison?’

CPDV.text: Who is left among you, who saw this house in its first glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not, in comparison to that, as nothing in your eyes?
CPDV.displayText: Who is left among you, who saw this house in its first glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not, in comparison to that, as nothing in your eyes?

verses.context: As the returned exiles rebuild the temple, Haggai asks those old enough to remember Solomon's temple whether this new one seems like nothing by comparison.

KJV.text: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts.
KJV.displayText: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts.

BSB.text: The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, declares the LORD of Hosts.
BSB.displayText: The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, declares the LORD of Hosts.

CPDV.text: Mine is the silver, and mine is the gold, says the Lord of hosts.
CPDV.displayText: Mine is the silver, and mine is the gold, says the Lord of hosts.

verses.context: Promising through Haggai to shake the nations and fill the unfinished temple with glory, God answers the builders' worry that their work looks poor and small.
